title: northstar-soleng-daily-docket
content:
Customer: Northstar Analytics (pilot, finance team).
Context: Dedicated deployment, want predictable 1000 qps bursts; compliance: PCI-SaaS subset. Private control plane + VPC peering requested.
Goals for next touchpoint (Wed 14:00 PT): finalize VPC CIDR decisions, get first e2e deployment running in staging, verify key rotation flow with their KMS.

Top-of-mind TODOs (ordered):
- [ ] Confirm CIDR allocation with Northstar infra (ask about overlapping 10.0/8 ranges) — ETA 1h (send 2 options: 10.40.0.0/16 or 10.128.0.0/16).
- [ ] Run staging deploy with nodepool size = 4 (A100s) + enable autoscale burst policy (test with load script).
- [ ] Validate KV/prefix cache integration on sequence lengths 512 (baseline) vs 128 (chat). Collect latency delta.
- [ ] Add canary rollout policy to route 10% traffic to quantized 4-bit variant (safety: fallback to full fp16).
- [ ] Demo KMS integration: test envelope key rotation using their AWS KMS ARN and our Private key proxy.
- [ ] Draft short runbook for on-call SEs: how to swap routes if model variant fails (include rollback command).

Notes / quick commands:
- k / kubectl quick: kubectl --context northstar-staging get pods -n redwood || kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/redwood-runtime --tail 200
- terraform: TF_VAR_region=us-west-2 TF_VAR_nodepool_size=4 make infra-deploy-staging
- load test (locally): python tools/bench/run_qps.py --target https://staging-ns.redwood/api --qps 600 --duration 2m --concurrency 50
- rollback model route: rbinctl route update --route policy-canary --weight 0 --model full-fp16 --env staging

Config snippets to keep handy (paste during screenshare):
- VPC peering note: create peering with route table entry to 10.40.0.0/16, set no-overlap check + accept from their account ID 111222333444
- Nodepool suggestion: gpu_type: a100-80gb
  node_count: 4
  scaling: min:2 max:12 target_cpu: 60

Troubleshooting checklist (if staging flaps during load):
1) Check runtime logs for OOM or CUDA errors -> grep "CUDA" /var/log/redwood/runtime.log
2) Confirm KV cache warming: curl -s staging/health/cache | jq .hit_rate
3) If latency spikes but CPU/GPU utilization low -> suspect bad batching policy. Try: rbinctl runtime set-batching --batch-size 8 --max-latency-ms 12
4) Network egress spike? Check VPC flow logs and NAT gateway quota (ask infra).

Customer-specific tradeoffs (notes from last call):
- They prefer predictable latency > raw throughput; willing to trade some throughput for lower p95. Emphasize autoscale + burst policy rather than purely larger nodepool.
- Compliance: they will insist on audit logs for KMS access and model route changes. Need to hook their SIEM (Splunk) via our audit stream.

Open questions to bring to solutions sync:
- Do we want to expose per-route cost-breakdown in the onboarding console for Northstar? (they asked for token cost estimate per endpoint)
- Can we default to synchronous key rotation test on staging before prod cutover? Ops/infra impact?

Meeting prep bullets (for Wed):
- 5m: quick recap + network CIDR options (ask if they have existing peering constraints)
- 10m: demo staging deploy + run brief load test showing p50/p95 before/after caching
- 10m: KMS rotation demo + explain audit logs and retention options
- 5m: next steps and timeline (deliverables: runbook, prod cutover checklist, 1-week post-cutover support window)

Personal notes / reminders:
- Send pre-meeting email with checklist and timeboxed expectations.
- Record staging run metrics to attach to Confluence page (p50/p95/cost per 1k tokens).
- Ask Sophie to draft the runbook skeleton (link to her doc in GH PR).

Past quick hits (reference):
- NS-8920: initial discovery notes (they want custom token retention set to 30 days)
- NS-9064: infra ask for private control plane (pending infra estimate)

End-of-day thought: try to keep demo simple — show clear before/after for caching. If we can cut p95 by 40% with minimal config changes that's a win for them.

-- AK
